monthly_review.summary: You've increased training intensity and efficiency this month, with faster paces, higher HR, and improved aerobic TE — but at the cost of reduced volume compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved by +0.64 m/sec per bpm — the largest positive shift across all metrics — indicating better cardiovascular economy at similar cadence.

goal_tracker.message: You need 4.6 more km across 1 remaining session to match last month’s distance — e.g., a single 5.0 km run at your April average pace (493 sec/km ≈ 8:13 min/km) would exceed the target.

insights.title: Efficiency gains outpacing pace gains
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.92 m/sec per bpm (+4.8%) while avg pace improved only 7.7% (534 → 493 sec/km), suggesting improved cardiac output utilization — especially notable given stable cadence.

insights.title: Shift toward higher-intensity work
insights.body: Zone 4 time increased from 12% to 21%, and Zone 5 from 1% to 6%, while Zone 2 dropped from 47% to 31% — indicating a clear strategic intensification, but potentially at the expense of foundational aerobic development.

insights.title: Stride length variability reflects pacing strategy
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 72.88 cm (slowest run, 9:08 min/km) to 91.78 cm (fastest run, 7:13 min/km) — a 26% increase — aligning with pace changes and showing healthy neuromuscular responsiveness; however, vertical oscillation remained consistently high (7.8–8.8 cm), suggesting opportunity for form refinement at faster efforts.

insights.title: Aerobic TE confirms effective stimulus
insights.body: Four of five recent runs had aerobic TE ≥ 3.0 (max 4.6), and April’s average (3.4) exceeds March’s (3.0) — confirming that even with fewer runs, each session delivered meaningful aerobic adaptation.

recommendations.action: Do one 5.0 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) before month-end, maintaining cadence ≥148 spm and vertical oscillation <8.0 cm (use real-time VO2 max/oscillation feedback on Garmin).
recommendations.reason: To restore Zone 2 volume lost this month (down 16% vs March) and support aerobic base without adding fatigue — critical given rising Z4/Z5 contribution and declining run count.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 × 800 m cruise interval at 428–440 sec/km (7:08–7:20 min/km), with 90 sec walk/jog recovery, focusing on stride length ≥88 cm and ground contact <305 ms.
recommendations.reason: Leverages your best recent pace (428 sec/km on 4/22) and strongest stride length (91.78 cm) to reinforce neuromuscular efficiency at threshold effort — supported by your elevated April aerobic TE (avg 3.4).

recommendations.action: Add 2 minutes of post-run dynamic mobility targeting hip flexors and calves, immediately after your next two runs — especially following any run with vertical oscillation >8.2 cm.
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation increased on your fastest (8.8 cm) and longest (8.4 cm) April runs, suggesting emerging fatigue or stiffness; targeted mobility can reduce oscillation drift and protect ground contact time (<310 ms).

weekly_focus.description: Balance intensity with recovery-focused volume to consolidate efficiency gains while stabilizing running economy across paces.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run (5 km, HR ≤135 bpm)
Recovery-pace easy run (4 km, HR 125–132 bpm) with form cues
